deals.headline: David Tepper pays a record $325m MLS expansion fee for Charlotte
deals.summary: MLS formally awarded its 30th franchise to Charlotte and Panthers owner David Tepper, who agreed to pay a record $325 million expansion fee; the Charlotte Business Journal reported he would invest $425 million in total including the fee, player and coaching salaries.

deals.date_text: December 2019 (commitment reported with the expansion award)
deals.evidence: Charlotte Mayor Vi Lyles has committed $110 million in city funding toward renovations that would make Bank of America Stadium suitable for pro soccer games
deals.headline: Charlotte commits $110m of city money for soccer-ready stadium works and a training facility
deals.summary: With the expansion award, Fox Business reported that Mayor Vi Lyles had committed $110 million in city funding toward renovations to make Bank of America Stadium suitable for MLS and toward a training facility. NFL.com later reported that the Charlotte FC practice-facility deal fell through; how much of the $110m was spent is not stated on these pages.

deals.date_text: Approved by Charlotte City Council 24 June 2024; bond financing authorised October 2025
deals.evidence: Under the policy document, the city will pay $650 million toward the renovation of Bank of America Stadium
deals.headline: Charlotte approves $650m of public money for Bank of America Stadium renovation
deals.investor: City of Charlotte (bonds repaid from hospitality and tourism taxes)
deals.summary: The City Council approved a joint $800 million renovation plan under which the city pays $650 million and David Tepper $150 million up front, keeping the Panthers in Charlotte through 2045; the city's share is funded from existing hospitality and tourism taxes, and in October 2025 the council authorised applying for $650 million of bond financing through the state (The Real Deal).

deals.evidence: The financial commitment includes $650 million from Tepper Sports & Entertainment, an increase from its original $150 million pledge
deals.headline: TSE raises its own stadium commitment to $650m, taking the project past $1.3bn through 2045
deals.summary: Tepper Sports & Entertainment said it will increase private investment in Bank of America Stadium to more than $1.3 billion through 2045, its own commitment rising to $650 million from the original $150 million alongside the city's $650 million; the agreement keeps the Panthers and Charlotte FC in Charlotte through 2045.

name: Charlotte Football Club
notes: US clubs publish no accounts: revenue ($85m) and operating income ($4m, EBITDA) are Forbes estimates for the 2025 MLS season, and the $740m value is Forbes' Feb 2026 MLS list (rank 12), cited via its Wayback Machine copy because forbes.com/sites blocks scripts; Charlotte is not in Forbes' May 2026 world top 30. Capacity is the stadium operator's specification figure for the whole venue (75,525, listed without a label on its stadium-info page; NFL.com calls it a 72,000-seat stadium); the smaller configuration Charlotte FC normally uses for MLS is not stated on a page read here. The expansion fee is recorded on the owner row as Tepper's entry amount. Stake percentage not disclosed (no other owner is reported). In Sept 2026 the Charlotte Business Journal reported Ally and the club in extension talks as the front-of-kit deal nears a decision. Legal entity is the ticket licensor named in the club's ticket terms; its registry number was not found. No league titles. Social follower counts not found.

owners.name: David Tepper (Tepper Sports & Entertainment)

ownership_summary: Charlotte FC is owned by David Tepper through Tepper Sports & Entertainment (TSE), which also owns the NFL's Carolina Panthers and Bank of America Stadium. MLS awarded Tepper the franchise on 17 December 2019 for a then-record $325m expansion fee; the club began play in 2022. No minority or institutional investor in the club is reported.
